questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was a good university, preferably with a Korean Studies Department. I ended up choosing Dageu, because it was smaller than Seoul, so I thought there would be more opportunities, for instance to join school clubs and so on. (which ended up being true!)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not easy regarding the dorms. Information about the dorms were given out super late, and it was not easy to find the building.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an intro-day, where we were informed about many important things like courses, school events, school jackets, alien registration card, opening up a Korean bank account and so on. And they also sent us the power point after. So that was really helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Several different dorms. I stayed in the female-only dorm, Hyupryuk-Hall. I shared a room with a girl from Norway.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were 3 meal plans available. I had the most extensive one including breakfast and dinner on weekdays, and also lunch on the weekends. In the beginning I liked the food, but eventually got tired of it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There is a curfew. You have to be home at 11:40PM everyday. Also weekends. If not, you have to apply online or on a paper slip, to stay out. But then you have to stay out all night, and cannot enter the dorm before 5AM. If you are even 1 minute late for curfew, you wil get penalty points.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The rooms were nice, two twin beds, lots of drawer and closet space, and a personal nice bathroom with shower. (in hyupryuk hall). I was very pleasantly surprised by the amount of storage space we had. (also a big shoe closet)  And personal desks of course!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Upon arrival was fine, but for me personally, in the first week having to apply for Master courses, I felt helpless, because no information was given about that. Only through my Korean buddy was I able to figure out what I was supposed to do, and it was a lengthy and frankly very over-complicated process to apply for the Master courses. I had to email professors if I could be in their class, and at that point it was really late, but luckily two Professors got back to me and accepted within the 48 hours I had to apply (in the add/drop period, mind you). Then I had to fill out a form in Korean, and attach screenshots of the acceptance from the Professors..  BUT, for normal students on the undergraduate level, they just had to apply online, and it seemed fairly easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My Korean buddy, and then emailing with the exchange coordinator. But she is extremely busy.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn't get any of the classes I though, but I was actually very happy with the classes I ended up with.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know, for Master's students, I guess email professors in advance and ask your buddy as soon as possible for help. For undergrads, definitely get up early and be ready for when the registration link opens, in order to get the classes you want. My roommate struggled a lot to figure out her schedule and get matching classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took MA classes, as I am a MA student.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: One class was very similiar, and the other was a bit different.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:

and

and

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Maybe school club fees? if you join a school club, there is a small fee, and if you want to go to their dinner parties and trips, you should set aside some money for that as well. Maybe for the trip to a cabin, it was like 300DKK?

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Doing laundry at the dorm was super cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were many clubs, and it was easy to join them!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I was in and English-club, and a volunteer club. My friend was in a women's football club, and there were also clubs like photography and astronomy etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Joining a club, and the school fall festival! So many cool concerts for free, and opportunities to talk to Korean students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Apsan Mountain. And Suseong Lake. And downtown, Dongseong-ro.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fine.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the clubs. And fight against your own shyness, and start up conversations with the memebers of the clubs.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Kindness and politeness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The dorms have curfew and are up on a hill. Walking from the subway station will be really hard.
Join the clubs. That's how I made Korean friends.
Enjoy, the campus is stunning!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The school also offers many free day trips to nearby cities, with cultural experiences and food.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting and socializing with so many Korean friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The registration process, haha. And not having a kitchen or a fridge.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
